doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

chapter: Big breaks: New Wave, Maynard, Tony Bennett
title: Leaving Maynard Ferguson; Eric Traub's nickname
summary: Refused a move from baritone, he gave notice; Eric Traub's nickname Zembo Mosque is recounted.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: there Migs left — Migliore left, and I asked if I could move to the alto chair and he wanted me on bari so he said no, and then Eric Traub left and I asked if I could move to the tenor chair and he said no I want to keep you on bari. That was the last straw.
There’s a name that I know from Fredonia. I’ll be darned.
Yeah his nickname was Zembo Mosque.

Zembo Mosque. That was the gig that we played when he first got on the band. That was the first gig. Zembo, some Mosque somewhere, and they nicknamed him that. But when I knew that I was destined to play bari forever with Maynard, I gave my notice and said I had to leave. And we left great friends too. There was no hassle there at all.
